page: Amazon Web Services m8i.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). It does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, requiring remote storage volumes for persistent data, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 2163.0, placing in the top quartile, complemented by strong throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 34.0 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.43 GB/sec. Geekbench text processing also registered in the upper 25% with a score of 2798.0. Multi-threaded workloads show moderate aggregate scaling due to the 2-core physical limit, reflected in an average Geekbench multi-core score of 4960.0 and a bottom-quartile stress-ng multi-core benchmark of 4319.66.

Memory and execution bandwidth remain solid for enterprise middle-tier tasks. Uncached memory reads and writes reach 44.57 GB/sec and 30.83 GB/sec respectively. Synthetic web serving throughput reached 8.43 GB/sec, while in-memory operations reached 7.62 million Redis SET operations per second. However, heavier compute loads such as medium-sized 7B parameter LLM text generation perform poorly at 5.04 tokens per second.

The Amazon Web Services m8i.xlarge offers balanced hardware density without local disk overhead. It is well suited for web serving, microservices, lightweight application backends, and moderate CI/CD compilation pipelines where per-core instruction efficiency is prioritized over high multi-threaded core counts.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory profile. It lacks local ephemeral storage and GPUs, relying on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps. The architecture supports modern vector extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-threaded execution, with high rankings in single-core Geekbench, text processing, and single-stream file compression. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng tests and larger 7B parameter LLM inference exhibit lower relative throughput due to the four-vCPU hardware ceiling. It is suited for web serving, microservices, and general application workloads requiring consistent single-core speed.
